title: Pass the CI reuse statement to the verifier; measure walltime
summary: After the checks step resolves a result record (CI or the local fallback), Athena builds `verify::reuse_statement` for the candidate SHA and puts it in the verifier's input, with a rule that the verifier doesn't re-run fmt, clippy or the full test suite for that SHA. The maintainer who owns the CI-routing design will judge it. The change records the walltime baseline with `xtask walltime` and states honestly that the "after" figure needs real post-change jobs.

defaults_applied.how: All changes are Rust, plus markdown docs.
New tests for the statement present/absent cases; the full cargo test and clippy must pass.
Judged by wall time per verified result with the same checks, not by wiring existing.
Criteria check that the statement reaches the verifier input and is withheld in stale/missing/red/build cases.
Wall-time figures come from xtask walltime or are labelled estimates.
A missing or blocked result gives no statement and no verified claim.
Docs and CHANGELOG are written for an outside reader.
One focused change; pushing the commit stays out.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Today `run.rs` calls `routing::run_routed` with `NoCi`, and `run_routed` returns only Vec<CheckRun>, so no record reaches the verifier. The change makes the resolved CiRecord (CI or local, keyed by SHA) available from the checks step and builds the statement from it.

Per 5.3 the local-fallback record is also reused by the verifier, so the statement is produced for local records too; with no pushed commit, every real job today gets a 'Athena's local run' statement, not a CI one. Pushing the commit is out of scope.

The statement goes into VerifierInputs (a new field or a CheckResultView entry) and into the verifier prompt rendering, with instructions to skip fmt/clippy/full test for that SHA but still run criterion-specific commands.
No statement is given when the SHA differs, the result is missing, the check is red, or the job is a build job (it never reuses a prior result).

The 'after' wall time cannot be measured in this change because it needs real jobs run after it lands. The 'before' is measured by running `cargo run --locked -p xtask -- walltime --capability change --last 20` on the available job records. If none are available, the docs say so. No speedup is claimed.
The goal is less duplicate verifier work for the same commit; the audience is the maintainer and the verifier agent.

acceptance_criteria.text: Unit tests show that, when the resolved record's SHA equals the candidate SHA, the verifier input contains the reuse statement (run address or local origin, SHA, per-check conclusions). Run `cargo test --locked` and check the new tests pass.
Tests show no statement is added for a different SHA, a missing or blocked result, a red result, or a `build` job, so the verifier keeps its full command set for those. Run `cargo test --locked`.

The rendered verifier brief or prompt tells the verifier that when the statement is present it must not re-run fmt, clippy or the full test suite for that SHA, must cite the statement in its report, and still runs criterion-specific commands and judges the criteria itself (design 6.1 and 6.2).

`run.rs` passes the record from the checks step into the verifier input in place of discarding it; `run_routed` or its caller exposes the record without weakening the red-is-red and local-fallback rules.

`docs/design/ci-routing.md` build item 5's 'Not done' no longer says the verifier's input lacks the reuse statement. It states what remains (no pushed commit, so the statement is currently the local record) and does not claim a speedup unless it was measured.

A measured 'before' wall time per verified result from `xtask walltime` is recorded in `docs/design/ci-routing-baseline.md` with the command, the sample size and the date. The 'after' is marked as not yet measurable, or is measured if enough post-change records exist. Any figure not measured is labelled an estimate.
`cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --all --check` are clean, and `cargo test --locked` passes in full.
CHANGELOG.md has an entry describing the change for an outside reader.

out_of_scope: Pushing the candidate commit and reading real CI runs (design 5.2 steps 1 to 3)
Cache and timeout-minutes work, and the CI wait bound's value
Per-phase timestamps in the job records
Claiming a speedup before post-change jobs exist
departures: The change spans three crates plus docs and a measurement step. The 'after' wall time can't be measured in this job, which raises the chance a verifier rejects the measurement criterion. So costs and times are above the reference and pass probability is below it.
